rounds.text: India Homes Ltd is exhibiting powerful fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 yielding a BUY recommendation with medium confidence [E65]. Profit growth has been robust, delivering a 25.4% CAGR over the last 5 years [E59], alongside a remarkable 219% growth in trailing twelve-month compounded profits [E21] and a net profit surge of 867% year-over-year [E66]. This earnings momentum is backed by extraordinary margin expansion, with operating margins reaching 82% in March 2026—a massive 510 percentage point improvement over three years—and a quarterly operating margin of 95% in March 2026 [E30, E31]. Furthermore, profitability metrics have turned exceptional in the latest period, highlighted by a current return on equity of 52.3% and an ROCE of 17.5% [E12, E13]. Market participants are increasingly validating this turnaround, as domestic institutional holdings have risen to 4.88% from 1.26%, driving positive money flow [E43, E44], while the stock achieves a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 alongside a 193.5% twelve-month price return [E51, E52]. Conceded: [E45], [E47], [E60], [E61], [E64].

The valuation of India Homes Ltd is stretched well beyond what the underlying fundamentals and historical track record support, trading at an aggressive P/E ratio of 46.2 and a price-to-book multiple of 19.20x [E1, E2]. This expensive pricing leaves no margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow model values the stock at Rs 19 against a market price of Rs 21.7, requiring an unsustainable 19.5% earnings growth rate merely to justify current levels [E45, E47]. Furthermore, the company carries severe leverage risks with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.02x where total borrowings exceed net worth, alongside potential red flags regarding the capitalization of interest costs [E38, E64]. Long-term operational performance displays deep historical shrinkage marked by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -27% and a deeply negative median return on equity of -14% over the same decade [E14, E26]. Promoter commitment is also waning and weak, with holdings dropping significantly by 15.86 percentage points since late 2023 down to just 34.25%, accompanied by extreme historical volatility reaching 226.7% and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.4% [E41, E53, E54]. Conceded: [E36], [E51].

The bear focuses excessively on high headline valuation multiples like a 46.2 P/E and 19.20x price-to-book [E1, E2], ignoring that current earnings are undergoing a massive acceleration where profit growth exceeded 1-year price growth by 76% [E57]. While the bear cites a DCF valuation of Rs 19 [E45], it glosses over the robust rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 pointing to a clear BUY with medium confidence [E65]. The criticism regarding historical shrinkage [E14] misses the dramatic 3-year turnaround showing a 74% compounded sales growth [E16] and a 37% compounded profit growth [E20]. Conceded: [E38], [E41]. Although leverage is highlighted [E38], actual borrowings successfully decreased to Rs 91 Cr from Rs 102 Cr [E39], while generating solid free cash flow of Rs 13 Cr [E36] alongside a stellar 100 relative-strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E51].

Conceded: [E16], [E20], [E39], [E51]. The bull cites accelerating profit growth and a strong relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51], but completely ignores that this price momentum has pushed the stock to trade at an extreme price-to-book of 19.20x versus a sector benchmark of just 2.37x [E7, E60]. While the bull highlights the rules-based screen score of 83 [E65], it glosses over the fundamental warning that today's market price of Rs 21.7 already demands an aggressive 19.5% earnings growth to justify itself, outstripping the base-case projection of 18.0% [E47]. The bull's reliance on recent margin expansion [E30, E31] and reduced borrowings [E39] masks severe structural baggage, including a long-term compounded sales contraction of -27% over 10 years [E14] and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.4% [E53]. Furthermore, the bull dismisses the bear's valuation concerns [E1, E2], yet the company carries a troubling debt-to-equity ratio of 2.02x where obligations exceed net worth [E38], alongside explicit flags that it might be capitalizing interest costs [E64].
